channel.title: NPR Topics: Education
channel.description: We've been to school. We know how education works. Right? In fact, many aspects of learning — in homes, at schools, at work and elsewhere — are evolving rapidly, along with our understanding of learning. Join us as we explore how learning happens.

item.title: Jason Arday, Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism, is found dead
item.description: Arday was 37 when he became Cambridge's youngest Black professor in 2023. He was found unresponsive Friday at a home in southwest London.

item.title: Judge dismisses Trump administration's antisemitism lawsuit against Harvard
item.description: A federal judge in Boston has dismissed a Trump administration lawsuit that claimed Harvard University did not do enough to protect students on campus from antisemitism.
item.content:encoded: A federal judge in Boston has dismissed a Trump administration lawsuit that claimed Harvard University did not do enough to protect students on campus from antisemitism.

item.title: Judge dismisses Trump administration lawsuit alleging antisemitism at Harvard University
item.description: The decision from U.S. District Judge Richard G. Stearns said that President Donald Trump's administration failed to prove an ongoing violation of federal civil rights laws.

item.title: How are schools adjusting sports for student athletes as sweltering heat lingers
item.description: As a new school year approaches, student athletes across Texas are returning to the field for fall sports, even as punishing heat lingers. How are rules and practices changing?

item.title: Trump administration proposes sweeping changes for Head Start, worrying advocates
item.description: The Trump administration is proposing new standards for Head Start, the nation's early education program for low-income kids. States would have a lot more control, and that has advocates worried.

item.title: Trump administration moves to deregulate Head Start, opening door for sweeping change
item.description: It would slim regulation of the 60-year-old anti-poverty program and aim to save money. Advocates worry the changes could undermine the early education program's mission.
